findings.title: Storage failures in Create and Update record metrics as legacy durations
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 45) and `DualWriterMode3.Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` is called instead of `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. Conversely, in `DeleteCollection` (line 166), the asynchronous `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call records its duration with `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This misattributes unified storage errors to legacy storage metrics and legacy delete-collection durations to unified storage metrics.

findings.title: Object name is passed as the kind label in Delete storage duration metric
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 106 calls `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passing the object `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the third argument (whereas line 103 and all other methods pass `options.Kind`). Aside from reporting the wrong label value, object names are unbounded per-resource identifiers, which introduces high-cardinality labels into the Prometheus metric.

findings.title: Asynchronous legacy writes use the request context and can be canceled when the HTTP handler returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the outer method returns immediately after the unified storage call completes, the HTTP server will finish the request and cancel `ctx`, which cancels the in-flight background `d.Legacy` operation before it finishes. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from parent cancellation (e.g. using `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)`).

findings.title: Asynchronous Legacy.Create shares and mutates the input object concurrently and loses generated fields
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, `d.Storage.Create` returns the newly created object `created` (which has generated name, UID, timestamps, and resourceVersion populated), while the background goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)` with the original `obj` (or if `Storage.Create` mutated `obj` in place, the caller/serializer may read `created` while `Legacy.Create` concurrently accesses or mutates the same struct). Furthermore, if a name was generated (e.g., via `generateName`), `obj` may not match `created` or may generate a different UID/name in legacy storage. A deep copy of `created` (or `obj`) should be passed to the background goroutine.

findings.title: Delete attaches the base logger to context instead of the enriched logger
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, line 96 constructs `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but line 97 passes `d.Log` instead of `log` to `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, losing the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log fields for downstream consumers of the context.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests race between background legacy goroutines and shared mock setup
findings.body: In `TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, and `TestMode3_Update`, both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` share the same `*mock.Mock` instance `m`, and the tests return immediately after `dw.<Method>` returns without synchronizing with the background goroutine launched by Mode 3. In `TestMode3_Delete` and `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, only ` m.On("Delete", ...)` once is configured, and in `TestMode3_Create`'s error case (lines 38-44) `setupLegacyFn` registers the expectation on `m` (which actually matches `us.Create` because `m` is shared). If the background goroutine runs concurrently with assertions or after the test finishes, `testify/mock` is accessed concurrently without synchronization or panics on unexpected calls.
